_about: The Apocalyptic theme's imagery side by side (plan 7.6b): images more than one book describes, each with the passages' own words (Berean Standard Bible, every quotation machine-checked), and two lines in the site's voice, Alike and Different, which say what the cells say and nothing more. Rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from links already judged (6.22 Revelation's links; 6.20 the prophets'); the Alike and Different lines read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet): 49 accepted, 25 revised, none withdrawn (ontology/provenance/briefs/7.6b-APOC-{ROWS,DRAFT,REVIEW}.md). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: Jeremiah & the Twelve: Jeremiah, Lamentations and Hosea-Malachi. Elsewhere: any other book.

rows.title: One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds, and the tribes who mourn

Daniel: One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven
Jeremiah & the Twelve: they will look on Me, the One they have pierced. They will mourn for Him
The land will mourn, each clan on its own
Gospels & letters: all the tribes of the earth will mourn
They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory
they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory
you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven
they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory
see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom
the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven
Revelation: He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him
all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him
One like the Son of Man
seated on the cloud was One like the Son of Man

rows.alike: Daniel sees "One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven"; the Gospel sayings speak of "the Son of Man coming" with clouds, Revelation 1:7 says "He is coming with the clouds", and Revelation 1:13 and 14:14 have "One like the Son of Man". Matthew 16:28 has "the Son of Man coming in His kingdom", and Matthew 26:64 has "the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven". Matthew 24:30 and Revelation 1:7 both say "all the tribes of the earth will mourn", and Zechariah 12:10 says of "the One they have pierced": "They will mourn for Him".
rows.different: The wording of the clouds varies: "with the clouds" (Daniel 7:13, Mark 14:62, Revelation 1:7), "on the clouds" (Matthew 24:30), "in the clouds" (Mark 13:26), "in a cloud" (Luke 21:27), "seated on the cloud" (Revelation 14:14); in Daniel the figure "approached the Ancient of Days" and "was led into His presence", while the Gospels say "they will see" him coming "with power and great glory", and Mark 14:62 adds "sitting at the right hand of Power". Matthew 16:28 says "coming in His kingdom" with no clouds, and Matthew 26:64 has "on the clouds of heaven" as Matthew 24:30 has "on the clouds". Zechariah 12:12 has "The land will mourn, each clan on its own" where Matthew and Revelation have "all the tribes of the earth".

rows.title: The man in linen: eyes like fire, limbs like polished bronze, a golden belt

Daniel: a certain man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist
his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze
I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground
Ezekiel: the soles of their feet were like the hooves of a calf, gleaming like polished bronze
Gospels & letters: His face shone like the sun
Revelation: dressed in a long robe, with a golden sash around His chest
His eyes were like a blazing fire
His feet were like polished bronze refined in a furnace
His face was like the sun shining at its brightest
I fell at His feet like a dead man
whose eyes are like a blazing fire and whose feet are like polished bronze
dressed in clean and bright linen and girded with golden sashes around their chests
He has eyes like blazing fire
His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire

rows.alike: Daniel's man is "dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold", with "eyes like flaming torches" and "arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze"; in Revelation 1 One "like the Son of Man" has "a golden sash around His chest", "His eyes were like a blazing fire" and "His feet were like polished bronze". Each seer falls down: Daniel "with my face to the ground", John "at His feet like a dead man".
rows.different: Daniel's belt is "around his waist" and Revelation 1:13's sash "around His chest"; Daniel has "arms and legs" of bronze where Revelation has "feet" (as Ezekiel 1:7 has "the soles of their feet"), and Daniel's face is "like the brilliance of lightning" where Revelation 1:16 has "like the sun shining at its brightest" (Matthew 17:2: "His face shone like the sun"; Revelation 10:1 says of "another mighty angel" that "His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire"). Revelation 1:13 says "a long robe", while linen and golden sashes appear in Revelation 15:6 on "the seven angels"; Daniel "fell into a deep sleep", John "like a dead man".

rows.title: A voice like the roar of many waters

Daniel: his voice like the sound of a multitude
Ezekiel: the sound of their wings like the roar of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army
His voice was like the roar of many waters
Revelation: His voice was like the roar of many waters
a sound from heaven like the roar of many waters and the loud rumbling of thunder
a sound like the roar of a great multitude, like the rushing of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder
a sound like the roar of a great multitude in heaven

rows.alike: Ezekiel 43:2 and Revelation 1:15 have the same words, "His voice was like the roar of many waters"; Ezekiel 1:24, Revelation 14:2 and Revelation 19:6 also compare a sound to "many waters". Revelation 19:1 and 19:6 both have "a sound like the roar of a great multitude".
rows.different: In Ezekiel 1:24 it is "the sound of their wings", set beside "the voice of the Almighty" and "the tumult of an army"; in Ezekiel 43:2 it is the voice of "the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east"; Revelation 14:2 and 19:6 add "thunder", and 14:2 adds "like harpists strumming their harps". Daniel 10:6 has "the sound of a multitude" and no waters, while Revelation 19:6 has both "a great multitude" and "many waters", and Revelation 19:1 has the multitude "in heaven" with no waters. Psalm 93:4 has "the roar of many waters" as the sea's own, with "the mighty breakers of the sea" and "the LORD on high" above them.

rows.title: Golden lampstands and two olive trees

Jeremiah & the Twelve: with a bowl at the top and seven lamps on it
There are also two olive trees beside it
These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth
the two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand
Elsewhere: a lampstand of pure, hammered gold
Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand
Revelation: These witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth

rows.alike: Each has golden lampstands: "a lampstand of pure, hammered gold" (Exodus), "a solid gold lampstand" (Zechariah), "seven golden lampstands" (Revelation 1:12). Zechariah 4 and Revelation 11:4 both have "two olive trees" and figures who stand by "the Lord of all the earth" / "the Lord of the earth".
rows.different: Exodus and Zechariah have one lampstand with "seven lamps"; Revelation 1:12 has "seven golden lampstands" and Revelation 11:4 "the two lampstands". Zechariah 4:14 says "These are the two anointed ones" "standing beside" the Lord, and Revelation 11:4 says "These witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands" that "stand before" Him.

rows.title: The sword or rod of His mouth

Isaiah: He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of His lips
He made My mouth like a sharp sword
Gospels & letters: whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth
Revelation: a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth
wage war against them with the sword of My mouth
from His mouth proceeds a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations

rows.alike: Each strikes or slays with something of the mouth: Isaiah 11:4 "He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth", 2 Thessalonians 2:8 "slay with the breath of His mouth", Revelation 19:15 "a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations".
rows.different: Isaiah 11:4 has "the rod of His mouth" and "the breath of His lips", 2 Thessalonians 2:8 "the breath of His mouth", and Revelation a "sword" that "came from His mouth" ("double-edged" in 1:16); in Isaiah 49:2 the speaker says "He made My mouth like a sharp sword". The ones struck are "the earth" and "the wicked" (Isaiah 11:4), "the lawless one" (2 Thessalonians 2:8), "them" (Revelation 2:16) and "the nations" (Revelation 19:15).

rows.title: The iron scepter that shatters like pottery

Elsewhere: I will make the nations Your inheritance
You will break them with an iron scepter; You will shatter them like pottery
Revelation: He will rule them with an iron scepter and shatter them like pottery
who will rule all the nations with an iron scepter
He will rule them with an iron scepter

rows.alike: Psalm 2:9 and Revelation 2:27 both have "an iron scepter" and "shatter them like pottery", and Revelation 12:5 and 19:15 repeat "with an iron scepter"; in each the ones ruled or broken are the nations.
rows.different: The Psalm says "You will break them" where Revelation says "He will rule them". The Psalm is spoken to "You", to whom "I will make the nations Your inheritance"; Revelation 2:26-27 says it of "the one who overcomes", Revelation 12:5 of "a male child", and Revelation 19:15 of the one from whose mouth "proceeds a sharp sword".

rows.title: Coming like a thief

Gospels & letters: in which watch of the night the thief was coming
at what hour the thief was coming
the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night
the Day of the Lord will come like a thief
Revelation: I will come like a thief, and you will not know the hour when I will come upon you
Behold, I am coming like a thief

rows.alike: Each speaks of a thief coming or of a coming like a thief's: "at what hour the thief was coming" (Luke 12:39), "will come like a thief in the night" (1 Thessalonians 5:2), "I will come like a thief" (Revelation 3:3); 1 Thessalonians 5:4 says "this day should overtake you like a thief". Matthew 24:43, Luke 12:39 and Revelation 3:3 speak of not knowing when ("in which watch of the night", "at what hour", "you will not know the hour"); Matthew 24:43 says the homeowner "would have kept watch", Revelation 3:3 "If you do not wake up", Revelation 16:15 "Blessed is the one who remains awake".
rows.different: In 1 Thessalonians 5:2 and 2 Peter 3:10 it is "the Day of the Lord" that will come like a thief; in 1 Thessalonians 5:4 it is said to "brothers" who "are not in the darkness"; in Revelation the speaker says "I will come" and "I am coming"; Matthew 24:43 and Luke 12:39 tell of "the homeowner" and a house "broken into". 2 Peter 3:10 adds "The heavens will disappear with a roar", and Revelation 16:15 adds "remains awake and clothed".

rows.title: The books opened and the Book of Life

Daniel: The court was convened, and the books were opened
everyone whose name is found written in the book
Gospels & letters: whose names are in the Book of Life
Elsewhere: blot me out of the book that You have written
Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book
blotted out of the Book of Life
Revelation: I will never blot out his name from the Book of Life
whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world
And books were opened, and one of them was the Book of Life
only those whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life
in the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain
not written in the Book of Life

rows.alike: Daniel 7:10 has "the books were opened" and Revelation 20:12 "books were opened", each with those who "stood before Him" or are "standing before the throne"; names "written in the book" (Daniel 12:1) or "in the Book of Life" (Philippians 4:3, Revelation) are spoken of, and Exodus 32:33, Psalm 69:28 and Revelation 3:5 all speak of blotting out of the book. Revelation 13:8, 17:8 and 20:15 speak of names not written in the Book of Life.
rows.different: Daniel 7:10 names no Book of Life, while Revelation 20:12 has "one of them was the Book of Life" and "the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books". Exodus 32:33 says "Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out", Psalm 69:28 asks that they "be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous", Revelation 3:5 "I will never blot out his name" of "he who overcomes"; Revelation 17:8 speaks of names "not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world" and 13:8 of names not written "from the foundation of the world" in "the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain"; Daniel 12:1 says those written "will be delivered", Revelation 20:15 says one not written in it "was thrown into the lake of fire", and Revelation 21:27 calls it "the Lamb's Book of Life".

rows.title: The key of David: what He opens no one can shut

Isaiah: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
Revelation: who holds the key of David. What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.
I have placed before you an open door, which no one can shut

rows.alike: Both have the same sentence about a key of David: "What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open."
rows.different: Isaiah has "the key to the house of David", which "I will place on his shoulder"; Revelation 3:7 has "the key of David", held by "the One who is holy and true", and Revelation 3:8 adds "an open door, which no one can shut".

rows.title: Oppressors come and bow down at your feet

Isaiah: they will come over in chains and bow down to you
They will bow to you facedown and lick the dust at your feet
The sons of your oppressors will come and bow down to you; all who reviled you will fall facedown at your feet
Revelation: I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will know that I love you

rows.alike: In each, others come and bow down before the one addressed: "come and bow down to you" and "fall facedown at your feet" (Isaiah 60:14), "lick the dust at your feet" (Isaiah 49:23), "come and bow down at your feet" (Revelation 3:9).
rows.different: Those who bow differ: "the Sabeans, men of stature" who "come over in chains" (Isaiah 45:14), "Kings" and "their queens" (Isaiah 49:23), "The sons of your oppressors" (Isaiah 60:14), and "those who belong to the synagogue of Satan, who claim to be Jews but are liars instead" (Revelation 3:9). What follows differs too: they confess "God is indeed with you" (Isaiah 45:14), "Then you will know that I am the LORD" (Isaiah 49:23), they "call you the City of the LORD" (Isaiah 60:14), and "they will know that I love you" (Revelation 3:9).

rows.title: Knocking at the door

Gospels & letters: when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once
Revelation: I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door

rows.alike: In each passage someone knocks and the door is to be opened: "My beloved is knocking", "when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him", "I stand at the door and knock".
rows.different: In the Song the one knocking speaks, "Open to me, my sister"; in Luke it is a master returning "from the wedding banquet" to waiting servants; in Revelation the one knocking says "I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me".

rows.title: Thrones set in place for judgment, myriads standing before Him

Daniel: thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat
Thousands upon thousands attended Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him
pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High
Gospels & letters: you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel
sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel
Revelation: I will grant the right to sit with Me on My throne
myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands
I saw the thrones, and those seated on them had been given authority to judge

rows.alike: Thrones are named with judging: "thrones were set in place" and "The court was convened" (Daniel 7:9-10), "sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (Matthew), "those seated on them had been given authority to judge" (Revelation). Daniel and Revelation count the throng with the same two numbers: "Thousands upon thousands" and "myriads upon myriads", "myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands".
rows.different: In Daniel 7:9 the one who takes his seat is "the Ancient of Days", and in 7:22 judgment is pronounced "in favor of the saints of the Most High"; Matthew numbers "twelve thrones" for "you who have followed Me", while Daniel 7:9 and Revelation 20:4 give no number. Daniel puts thousands before myriads and says they "stood before Him"; Revelation 5:11 puts "myriads of myriads" first and has the angels "encircling the throne".

rows.title: The throne and the living creatures

Daniel: His throne was flaming with fire
Ezekiel: the form of four living creatures
the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle
glowing coals of fire, or of torches
all four rims were full of eyes all around
an awesome expanse, gleaming like crystal
on the throne high above was a figure like that of a man
like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day
Their entire bodies, including their backs, hands, and wings, were full of eyes all around
All four living creatures had faces and wings
Isaiah: I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted
Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts
Elsewhere: a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself
Revelation: I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it
a rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne
Before the throne burned seven torches of fire
something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal
four living creatures, covered with eyes in front and back
The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf, the third had a face like a man, and the fourth was like an eagle in flight.
each of the four living creatures had six wings
Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty
encircled by the four living creatures and the elders
the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb
one of the four living creatures say in a voice like thunder
a voice from among the four living creatures
around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures
before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders
one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls
the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne

rows.alike: Ezekiel and Revelation both see one seated on a throne with "four living creatures", a rainbow around the seated One (Ezekiel 1:28) or the throne (Revelation 4:3), fire like "torches", something "gleaming like crystal" or "as clear as crystal", and eyes "all around"; the creatures' likenesses are lion, ox or calf, man and eagle in both. Isaiah's seraphim and Revelation's four living creatures each have six wings, and both are heard calling "Holy, holy, holy". "All four living creatures had faces and wings" in Ezekiel 1:8, and the four living creatures are with the throne again in Revelation 5:6, 5:8, 5:14, 7:11, 14:3 and 19:4.
rows.different: In Ezekiel each creature has four faces, "the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle", and Ezekiel 1:8 adds "human hands" under their wings, while in Revelation "The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf"; Ezekiel's eyes are on the "rims" and on their "entire bodies", Revelation's are "in front and back" and "all around and within". Ezekiel's throne has "the appearance of sapphire" and Exodus's pavement is "made of sapphire", while Revelation's seated One "looked like jasper and carnelian"; Isaiah's cry is "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts", Revelation's "Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty". In Revelation 6:1 one of the creatures says "Come!", in 6:6 "a voice from among" them speaks, and in 15:7 one of them "gave the seven angels seven golden bowls".

rows.title: The sealed scroll and the words sealed up

Daniel: you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future
shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end
the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end
the wicked will continue to act wickedly
Ezekiel: written on the front and back of it
Isaiah: like the words sealed in a scroll
Revelation: It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals
Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down
Do not seal up the words of prophecy in this book, because the time is near
Let the unrighteous continue to be unrighteous

rows.alike: A scroll is written on both sides ("written on the front and back of it", "writing on both sides") and words are sealed ("the words sealed in a scroll", "seal the book", "sealed with seven seals"). Daniel and Revelation both follow a word about sealing with the wicked going on as they are: "the wicked will continue to act wickedly", "Let the unrighteous continue to be unrighteous".
rows.different: Daniel is told to "seal the book until the time of the end" and to "seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future"; Revelation 10:4 says "Seal up what the seven thunders have said", but Revelation 22:10 says "Do not seal up the words of prophecy in this book, because the time is near". Ezekiel's scroll is unrolled and holds "words of lamentation, mourning, and woe"; Revelation's has "seven seals"; Isaiah's reader says "I cannot, because it is sealed".

rows.title: The scroll that is eaten

Ezekiel: a hand reaching out to me, and in it was a scroll
So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth
Jeremiah & the Twelve: Your words were found, and I ate them
Elsewhere: sweeter than honey in my mouth
Revelation: He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open
ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter

rows.alike: In Ezekiel and Revelation a scroll is in a hand, the seer is told to eat it, and both say "it was as sweet as honey in my mouth". Jeremiah says of God's words "I ate them", and the psalm calls them "sweeter than honey in my mouth".
rows.different: Revelation adds "my stomach turned bitter", which Ezekiel 3:3 does not have; Ezekiel is to "go and speak to the house of Israel", while Revelation's is a "small scroll" taken "from the angel's hand". Jeremiah eats "Your words" rather than a scroll, and they became "my joy and my heart's delight".

rows.title: A hand raised to heaven in an oath

Daniel: raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven
swear by Him who lives forever
Elsewhere: I lift up My hand to heaven
Revelation: lifted up his right hand to heaven
he swore by Him who lives forever and ever

rows.alike: A hand is lifted to heaven with an oath on living forever: "raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven" and "swear by Him who lives forever" (Daniel), "lifted up his right hand to heaven" and "swore by Him who lives forever and ever" (Revelation), "I lift up My hand to heaven" (Deuteronomy).
rows.different: Daniel's man in linen raises "his right hand and his left hand", Revelation's angel "his right hand"; in Deuteronomy the speaker swears by his own life, "As surely as I live forever". Daniel's figure is "above the waters of the river" and swears "It will be for a time, and times, and half a time"; Revelation's is "standing on the sea and on the land" and swears "There will be no more delay!"

rows.title: The Lion of Judah and the Root of Jesse

Isaiah: a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse
the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples
Gospels & letters: The Root of Jesse will appear
Revelation: the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David
I am the Root and the Offspring of David

rows.alike: A lion is tied to Judah ("Judah is a young lion", "the Lion of the tribe of Judah"), and a Root to Jesse or David ("the Root of Jesse", "the Root of David").
rows.different: Genesis says of Judah himself, "Judah is a young lion", where Revelation has "the Lion of the tribe of Judah". Isaiah and Romans say "Root of Jesse", Revelation "Root of David" and "the Root and the Offspring of David"; Isaiah 11:10 says the Root "will stand as a banner for the peoples", Romans, quoting Isaiah, "will appear".

rows.title: The lamb led to the slaughter

Isaiah: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter
Gospels & letters: Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world
He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent
Revelation: a Lamb who appeared to have been slain

rows.alike: A lamb and slaughter: "led like a lamb to the slaughter" (Isaiah), "a Lamb who appeared to have been slain" (Revelation); John calls Jesus "the Lamb of God".
rows.different: Isaiah has "like a lamb to the slaughter" and "as a sheep before her shearers"; Acts, giving the passage the eunuch was reading, has "like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer". Revelation's Lamb is "standing in the center of the throne" with "seven horns and seven eyes"; John's Lamb "takes away the sin of the world".

rows.title: Seven eyes ranging over all the earth

Jeremiah & the Twelve: these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth
Elsewhere: the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth
Revelation: seven eyes, which represent the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth

rows.alike: Eyes go out over the whole earth: "roam to and fro over all the earth", "scan the whole earth", "sent out into all the earth".
rows.different: Zechariah and Revelation number them "seven" and 2 Chronicles gives no number. In 2 Chronicles and Zechariah they are "the eyes of the LORD"; in Revelation the Lamb "had seven horns and seven eyes", and the verse goes on "the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth".

rows.title: The golden altar, the censer, and incense as prayer

Ezekiel: Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city
Isaiah: a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar
Gospels & letters: standing at the right side of the altar of incense
I stand in the presence of God
Elsewhere: an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense
Overlay with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns
Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony
take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD
May my prayer be set before You like incense
He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood
the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense to make atonement for Israel
refined gold for the altar of incense
to burn incense on the altar of incense
with a censer in his hand to offer incense
Revelation: golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints
the seven angels who stand before God
another angel, who had a golden censer, came and stood at the altar
on the golden altar before the throne
filled it with fire from the altar, and hurled it to the earth

rows.alike: A gold altar of incense stands "in front of the ark of the Testimony" (Exodus 40:5) and "the golden altar before the throne" (Revelation 8:3), a censer is filled with fire from the altar ("a censer full of burning coals from the altar", "took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar"), and incense is joined to prayer ("May my prayer be set before You like incense", "incense, which are the prayers of the saints"). Hebrews 9:4 has "the golden altar of incense", and Exodus 37:25, 1 Chronicles 6:49, 1 Chronicles 28:18 and 2 Chronicles 26:16 speak of "the altar of incense".
rows.different: In Leviticus the coals and incense are taken "inside the veil", in Revelation the angel "hurled it to the earth"; Ezekiel's coals come "from among the cherubim" to be scattered "over the city", and Isaiah's coal is taken "with tongs" by one of the seraphim. The psalm says prayer is "like incense", Revelation that the bowls of incense "are the prayers of the saints"; Luke's angel stands "at the right side of the altar of incense", Revelation's "stood at the altar" with "a golden censer". Exodus 37:25 says it was made "out of acacia wood"; 1 Chronicles 6:49 has offerings on it "to make atonement for Israel"; 2 Chronicles 26:19 has Uzziah "with a censer in his hand to offer incense" before "the altar of incense", and "leprosy broke out on his forehead".

The further inability differs too: "eat or smell" (Deuteronomy 4:28), "understand" (Daniel), "walk" (Revelation, as in Psalm 115's "they have feet, but cannot walk").

rows.alike: Revelation's angel is "wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow above his head" and his "legs were like pillars of fire"; Genesis has "My rainbow in the clouds" and Exodus "a pillar of cloud" and "a pillar of fire."
rows.different: In Genesis the rainbow is set "in the clouds" as "a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth"; in Revelation it is "above his head" of "another mighty angel." In Exodus "the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud" to guide them; in Revelation the angel is "wrapped in a cloud" while "coming down from heaven."

rows.title: The measuring rod

he measured the city with the rod

rows.alike: In each a measuring instrument is held and something is measured: Ezekiel's man has "a measuring rod in his hand" and in Ezekiel 42:16 "With a measuring rod he measured the east side", Zechariah's "a man with a measuring line in his hand" goes "To measure Jerusalem", and in Revelation there is "a measuring rod like a staff" and "a golden measuring rod to measure the city."
rows.different: Ezekiel's man holds both "a linen cord and a measuring rod" and measures "the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high"; Zechariah's is to determine Jerusalem's "width and length"; in Revelation 11:1 the rod is given to the seer to "measure the temple of God and the altar, and count the number of worshipers", and in Revelation 21 the angel's rod is "golden", the wall "144 cubits" and the city "12,000 stadia in length and width and height."

rows.title: The holy city trampled

Daniel: the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled

Revelation: it has been given over to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for 42 months

rows.alike: Each speaks of something trodden underfoot: "the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled" (Daniel), "Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles" (Luke), "they will trample the holy city" (Revelation).

rows.title: Fire from heaven and the sky shut

Gospels & letters: the sky was shut for three and a half years

rows.title: The breath of life enters and they stand on their feet

Revelation: celebrate and send one another gifts

rows.alike: In both the seer answers by saying the one speaking to him knows: to "can these bones come to life?" Ezekiel says "only You know", and in Revelation 7:14 "I answered, 'you know.'"
rows.different: Ezekiel addresses "O Lord GOD" and says "only You know"; in Revelation he addresses "Sir", and the one he answered then gives the answer himself: "These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation".

rows.title: Beasts from the sea, ten horns, and a mouth speaking arrogant words

rows.title: An image set up to be worshipped on pain of death

whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace
Revelation: make an image to the beast
cause all who refused to worship it to be killed

rows.alike: In both an image is made, and those who will not worship it are to be thrown into a furnace (Daniel 3:6: "whoever does not fall down and worship") or killed (Revelation 13:15: "all who refused to worship it").
rows.different: In Daniel "King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide" and refusers are "thrown into the blazing fiery furnace"; in Revelation those on the earth are told "to make an image to the beast", the second beast gives it breath "so that the image could speak", and refusers are "to be killed".

rows.title: The kings of the earth gathered for battle

Jeremiah & the Twelve: I will gather all the nations
to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms

Revelation: the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ
all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle
the kings of the earth with their armies assembled to wage war

rows.alike: Kings and nations are gathered together: "The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together" (Psalm 2:2, Acts 4:26), "I will gather all the nations for battle" (Zechariah 14:2), "the kings of the earth with their armies assembled" (Revelation 19:19).
rows.different: Who gathers them differs: in Psalm 2:2 the kings gather themselves "against the LORD and against His Anointed One"; in Joel and Zechariah the LORD says "I will gather", and in Zephaniah "My decision is to gather nations"; in Revelation 16:14 "demonic spirits" go out "to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty". Zechariah's battle is "against Jerusalem"; Revelation 19:19's is "against the One seated on the horse, and against His army".

rows.title: A woman in labour gives birth to a son

Isaiah: As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain
she gave birth; before she was in pain, she delivered a boy
as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children
Jeremiah & the Twelve: until she who is in labor has given birth
Elsewhere: the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me
Revelation: a woman clothed in the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head
crying out in the pain and agony of giving birth
she gave birth to a son, a male child
the woman who was about to give birth

rows.alike: A woman in labour cries out: "writhes and cries out in pain" (Isaiah 26:17), "crying out in the pain and agony of giving birth" (Revelation 12:2); and gives birth to a son: "she delivered a boy" (Isaiah 66:7), "she gave birth to a son, a male child" (Revelation 12:5). Isaiah 66:8 has Zion "in labor" who "gave birth to her children", and Revelation 12:4 has "the woman who was about to give birth". Sun, moon and stars appear together in Genesis 37:9 and Revelation 12:1.
rows.different: Isaiah 66:7's woman gives birth "Before she was in labor" and "before she was in pain", while Revelation 12:2's is "crying out in the pain" before the birth; Isaiah 26:17 is a comparison ("so were we in Your presence, O LORD"). Joseph's dream has "eleven stars" "bowing down to me"; Revelation's woman wears "a crown of twelve stars".

rows.title: The earth opens its mouth and swallows

Revelation: opened its mouth to swallow up the river

rows.alike: In both the earth swallows: "the earth swallowed them up" (Exodus 15:12); the earth "opened its mouth to swallow up the river" (Revelation 12:16).
rows.different: In Exodus the earth swallows "them" when "You stretched out Your right hand"; in Revelation "the earth helped the woman" and swallows "the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth".

rows.title: Firstfruits

Jeremiah & the Twelve: Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest
Revelation: redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb

rows.alike: Both call a people "firstfruits": "the firstfruits of His harvest" (Jeremiah 2:3), "firstfruits to God and to the Lamb" (Revelation 14:4).
rows.different: Jeremiah says "Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest" and "All who devoured her were found guilty"; Revelation 14:4 says "These are the ones who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins", "They follow the Lamb wherever He goes", and "They have been redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb."

rows.title: The cup of the wine of wrath, and Babylon's golden cup

Jeremiah & the Twelve: this cup of the wine of wrath
Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD
Elsewhere: a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices
Revelation: made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her immorality
the wine of God's anger, poured undiluted into the cup of His wrath
the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath
She held in her hand a golden cup
All the nations have drunk the wine

rows.alike: A cup of wine is the LORD's wrath: "a cup is in the hand of the LORD" (Psalm 75:8), "the cup of His fury" (Isaiah 51:17), "this cup of the wine of wrath" (Jeremiah 25:15), "the cup of His wrath" (Revelation 14:10). The nations drink Babylon's wine: "The nations drank her wine" (Jeremiah 51:7), "All the nations have drunk the wine" (Revelation 18:3).
rows.different: In Jeremiah 51:7 "Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD"; in Revelation 17:4 the woman "held in her hand a golden cup full of abominations", and in 16:19 God "gave her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath". The Psalm's wine is "mixed with spices" and Revelation 14:10's "poured undiluted"; the drinker is Jerusalem in Isaiah 51:17 and "all the nations to whom I send you" in Jeremiah 25:15.

Isaiah: I have trodden the winepress alone
their blood spattered My garments, and all My clothes were stained
Jeremiah & the Twelve: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe
Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full
Revelation: gathered the grapes of the earth, and he threw them into the great winepress of God's wrath
the winepress was trodden outside the city
He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood
He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty

rows.alike: A sickle is swung over a ripe harvest: "Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe" (Joel 3:13), "Swing Your sickle and reap" and "the crop of the earth is ripe" (Revelation 14:15); and a winepress is trodden by one whose clothes bear blood: "I have trodden the winepress alone" and "their blood spattered My garments" (Isaiah 63:3), "He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood" and "He treads the winepress" (Revelation 19:13, 15).
rows.different: In Revelation 14:15 an angel calls "to the One seated on the cloud" and in 14:19 "the angel swung his sickle over the earth"; Joel's call is "Come, trample the grapes". Isaiah's treader says "no one from the nations was with Me"; Revelation 14:20 adds that the winepress was trodden "outside the city" and the blood rose "as high as the bridles of the horses for a distance of 1,600 stadia".

rows.title: The temple filled with smoke and glory

Ezekiel: The temple was filled with the cloud
the glory of the LORD filling His temple
Isaiah: the temple was filled with smoke
Elsewhere: the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle
Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting
the cloud filled the house of the LORD
the priests could not stand there to minister
Revelation: the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God
no one could enter the temple

rows.alike: The sanctuary is filled: "the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle" (Exodus 40:34), "the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD" (1 Kings 8:11), "the temple was filled with smoke" (Isaiah 6:4, Revelation 15:8); and in Exodus, 1 Kings and Revelation people are kept from their place in it: "Moses was unable to enter", "the priests could not stand there to minister", "no one could enter the temple".
rows.different: Exodus 40:34 has "the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting", 1 Kings 8:10 "the cloud filled the house of the LORD" and Ezekiel 10:4 "The temple was filled with the cloud", while Isaiah 6:4 and Revelation 15:8 have "smoke"; Revelation's smoke is "from the glory of God and from His power". Revelation says no one could enter "until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed"; Exodus says Moses could not "because the cloud had settled on it".

rows.title: The Euphrates dried up

Isaiah: He will sweep His hand over the Euphrates
He will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals
Jeremiah & the Twelve: A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up
Revelation: the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up

rows.alike: Each speaks of water dried up or divided: Isaiah 11:15 has the Euphrates split "for men to cross with dry sandals", Jeremiah 50:38 says "A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up", and Revelation 16:12 says of "the great river Euphrates" that "its water was dried up".
rows.different: In Isaiah the LORD acts "with a scorching wind" and splits the river "into seven streams"; in Revelation "the sixth angel poured out his bowl" and the drying is "to prepare the way for the kings of the East". Jeremiah 50:38 names "a drought" and does not name the Euphrates in the verse.

Ezekiel: the music of your lyres will no longer be heard

the birds of prey will gather

come out from it, purify yourselves

in a moment, in a single day
in spite of your many sorceries
Jeremiah & the Twelve: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered
the desert creatures and hyenas will live there

Come out of her, My people!
her judgment extends to the sky and reaches to the clouds
as she has done, do the same to her
do to her as she has done
repay them double their iniquity and their sin
will shout for joy over Babylon

the voices of the bride and bridegroom

the voices of the bride and bridegroom
the voices of the bride and bridegroom

Elsewhere: repays you as you have done to us
Revelation: Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great
a haunt for every unclean spirit, every unclean bird, and every detestable beast
Come out of her, My people
her sins are piled up to heaven

pay her back double for what she has done

the sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, will never ring out in you again

the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again

rows.alike: Isaiah 21:9 cries "Fallen, fallen is Babylon!" and Revelation 14:8 and 18:2 "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great", and Revelation 16:19 says "God remembered Babylon the great"; Jeremiah 51:45 and Revelation 18:4 both say "Come out of her, My people", and the fallen city becomes "a haunt for jackals" in Jeremiah 51:37 and "a haunt for every unclean spirit, every unclean bird, and every detestable beast" in Revelation 18:2. The sounds of joy, "the voices of the bride and bridegroom", are also taken away in Jeremiah: in 7:34 the LORD says "I will remove from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem the sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of the bride and bridegroom", and in 25:10 "I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp"; Revelation 18:22-23 says the sound of a millstone, the light of a lamp and the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never be heard or seen "in you again".
rows.different: Jeremiah 51:63 has a stone tied to "this scroll" and cast "into the Euphrates"; Revelation 18:21 has "a mighty angel" cast "a stone the size of a great millstone" "into the sea". In Isaiah 47 the one addressed says "I will be queen forever" and is told "loss of children, and widowhood" will overtake her "in a single day"; in Revelation 18:7 she says "I sit as queen" and her plagues come "in one day" as "death and grief and famine"; and where Psalms 137:8 and Jeremiah 50:29 repay her as she has done, Revelation 18:6 adds "pay her back double".

rows.title: The prostitute who sits on many waters

Ezekiel: your remnant will be consumed by fire

the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery

The kings of the earth were immoral with her

rows.different: In Revelation 17:16 it is "the ten horns and the beast" who hate her and "eat her flesh"; in Ezekiel 16:39 it is "your lovers" who leave her naked, and in 2 Kings 9:36 "the dogs" devour "the flesh of Jezebel". Isaiah 23:17 names Tyre, who will "sell herself to all the kingdoms", and Nahum 3:4 a "mistress of sorcery" who "betrays nations"; Revelation has "The kings of the earth" immoral with her and adds "a golden cup full of abominations".

gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones

cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; of fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet

all who had ships on the sea were enriched by her wealth
your merchants were the great ones of the earth

rows.alike: In both, kings, merchants and seafarers mourn a city: Ezekiel's "sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore" and Revelation's "Every shipmaster, passenger, and sailor" "will stand at a distance"; Ezekiel's lament asks "Who was ever like Tyre" and Revelation's "What city was ever like this great city?" rows.different: Ezekiel names "Tyre" and her trading partners; Revelation names "the mighty city of Babylon", and its mourners watch "the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her" and say "in a single hour your judgment has come". Ezekiel's mourners "shave their heads" and "wrap themselves in sackcloth", Revelation's "throw dust on their heads"; in Ezekiel 27:33 she "enriched the kings of the earth", in Revelation 18:19 "all who had ships on the sea were enriched".

rows.title: A bride adorned for her husband

as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride
Revelation: His bride has made herself ready
She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure
prepared as a bride adorned for her husband

Revelation: cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead

rows.alike: Both summon birds to a meal, Ezekiel's "great feast" and Revelation's "great supper of God", to eat "horses and riders" and "mighty men", and both use the word "gorged".
rows.different: Ezekiel calls "every beast of the field" as well as birds, names a "sacrificial feast" "on the mountains of Israel", and adds "drink blood until you are drunk"; Revelation calls "all the birds" through "an angel standing in the sun", adds "kings and commanders" and "everyone slave and free, small and great", and reports that "all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh".

Daniel: The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found
Revelation: Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them

rows.alike: In both, what was there can no longer be found: Daniel's "not a trace of them could be found" and Revelation's "no place was found for them".
rows.different: In Daniel it is "the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold" of the statue, which "became like chaff" and were carried off by "The wind", and "the stone" then "filled the whole earth"; in Revelation it is "Earth and heaven", which "fled from His presence" before "a great white throne".

rows.title: The holy city: on a high mountain, foursquare, its gates, foundations and light

the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel
4,500 cubits on the north side, 4,500 cubits on the south side, 4,500 cubits on the east side, and 4,500 cubits on the west side
Isaiah: all your walls of precious stones
No longer will the sun be your light by day
the LORD will be your everlasting light
they will never be shut, day or night
the wealth of the nations will come to you
the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you
Gospels & letters: built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets
Elsewhere: a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst
each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes
twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high
engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes
Revelation: a mountain great and high, and showed me the holy city
twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel
twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb

12,000 stadia in length and width and height
the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst
the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it
Its gates will never be shut

rows.alike: Ezekiel is set "on a very high mountain" and John on "a mountain great and high" to see a city whose gates bear the names of "the tribes of Israel", measured the same on every side; Isaiah's city, like Revelation's, has gates that "will never be shut", needs no "sun" for its light, has foundations of "sapphires", receives the wealth of "the nations", and is not entered by the "unclean".
rows.different: Ezekiel's city measures "4,500 cubits" on each of four sides and 1 Kings 6:20's inner sanctuary "twenty cubits" each way, where Revelation's city is "12,000 stadia in length and width and height"; Revelation's foundations bear "the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb", while Ephesians 2:20 has "the foundation of the apostles and prophets" and Exodus 28:21 and 39:14 set the names of the twelve tribes on stones, "engraved like a seal". Isaiah 60:19 says "the LORD will be your everlasting light"; Revelation 21:23 says "the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp".

rows.title: A new name

Isaiah: You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow
to His servants He will give another name
Revelation: a white stone inscribed with a new name

rows.alike: Both speak of a new name given: Isaiah's "a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow" and "another name" for "His servants", Revelation's "a white stone inscribed with a new name" for "the one who overcomes".
rows.different: Revelation 2:17 puts the name on "a white stone", "known only to the one who receives it", and 3:12 writes on the overcomer "the name of My God", "the name of the city of My God" and "My new name"; Isaiah 62:2 adds "Nations will see your righteousness", and 65:15 sets the servants' "another name" against "your name as a curse".

rows.title: The abomination of desolation

Daniel: set up the abomination of desolation
the abomination of desolation set up
Gospels & letters: spoken of by the prophet Daniel
the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be

rows.alike: Daniel 11:31 and 12:11, Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14 all use the words "the abomination of desolation", and Daniel 9:27 has "the abomination that causes desolation"; Matthew names it as "spoken of by the prophet Daniel".
rows.different: Daniel sets it beside the ending of sacrifice ("abolish the daily sacrifice", "the daily sacrifice is abolished"), places it "on the wing of the temple" in 9:27, and counts "1,290 days" in 12:11; Matthew has it "standing in the holy place" and Mark "standing where it should not be", and both add "let the reader understand", with Mark going on "let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains".

rows.title: Heaven is My throne, earth My footstool

Isaiah: Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool
What kind of house will you build for Me?
Gospels & letters: by heaven, for it is God's throne
or by the earth, for it is His footstool
Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool
What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord
Elsewhere: build for Me a house to dwell in

rows.alike: All three call heaven a throne and the earth a footstool: Isaiah has "Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool", and Matthew has "by heaven, for it is God's throne" and "by the earth, for it is His footstool". Isaiah and Acts both go on to ask "What kind of house will you build for Me?", and 2 Samuel 7:5 has "Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?"
rows.different: Isaiah and Acts speak in the first person ("My throne", "My footstool"), while Matthew speaks of "God's throne" and "His footstool" in a command "not to swear at all" and adds "or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King". Isaiah opens "This is what the LORD says", where Acts places "says the Lord" inside the question.

rows.title: Their worm will never die, their fire never quenched

Isaiah: their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched
Gospels & letters: their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched

rows.alike: Both speak of a worm that does not die and a fire that is not quenched: "their worm will never die" (Isaiah) and "their worm never dies" (Mark).
rows.different: Isaiah has "their fire will never be quenched" and Mark "the fire is never quenched". Isaiah sets the words beside "the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me" who "will be a horror to all mankind"; Mark introduces them with "where".

rows.title: The messenger who prepares the way

Isaiah: Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness
make a straight highway for our God in the desert
prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people
prepare the way for the people
Jeremiah & the Twelve: I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me
Gospels & letters: A voice of one calling in the wilderness
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You
Elsewhere: prepare the way for His steps
Revelation: prepare the way for the kings of the East

rows.alike: Each has a way prepared: "Prepare the way for the LORD" (Isaiah, and "Prepare the way for the Lord" in Matthew, Mark and Luke 3:4), and a sent messenger "who will prepare the way" (Malachi; "who will prepare Your way" in Matthew, Mark and Luke 7:27). Luke 1:76 says a child "will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him".
rows.different: Isaiah has "Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness" and "make a straight highway for our God in the desert", where Matthew and Mark have "A voice of one calling in the wilderness" and "make straight paths for Him". Malachi's messenger prepares the way "before Me"; in Matthew and Mark the messenger is sent "ahead of You" to prepare "Your way".

rows.title: Elijah sent before the day

Jeremiah & the Twelve: I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD
he will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children
Gospels & letters: he is the Elijah who was to come
Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things
in the spirit and power of Elijah
to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children

rows.alike: Each speaks of Elijah coming: "I will send you Elijah the prophet" (Malachi), "the Elijah who was to come" (Matthew 11:14), "Elijah does indeed come" (Matthew 17:11). Malachi and Luke share the words "turn the hearts of the fathers to their children".
rows.different: Malachi continues "and the hearts of the children to their fathers", where Luke continues "and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous". Malachi names "Elijah the prophet" coming "before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD"; Luke has "in the spirit and power of Elijah", and Matthew 17:11 adds "he will restore all things".
